title: DiffusionEdge: Diffusion Probabilistic Model for Crisp Edge Detection
mechanism: A latent diffusion edge detector. A pixel-level, uncertainty-aware cross-entropy is distilled into the latent space, with an adaptive Fourier filter, and it predicts crisp edges without NMS.
adaptation: Train on binary crack and gridline maps with the 1-channel EL image replicated, at 512 px. First check that the autoencoder can reconstruct the 1 px GT crack maps, a cheap test. Mainly a benchmark baseline for generative thin-structure methods.
min_experiment: Gate: autoencoder reconstruction IoU of GT crack maps, which must be >= 0.9 to proceed. Arm: DiffusionEdge on crack, 3 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: relF1@2, crack IoU. Kill at the gate or if relF1@2 is more than 0.03 below the house model.
evidence: R: on NYUDv2, ODS +30.2%, OIS +28.1% and AC +65.1% over the second best without post-processing. Trained on benchmark-sized sets of a few hundred to a thousand images.
prior_overlap: Diffusion segmenters are listed as never tried. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Train on crack + gridline binary maps, 1-channel replicated, 512 px; check VAE reconstruction of 1 px cracks first. Mainly the generative member of the benchmark suite.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: DiffusionEdge on 478 cells, 2 seeds; baseline house. Metrics relF1@2, crack IoU, AC. Kill if relF1@2 below house - 0.02. About 30 GPU-h.
